what: The Verify Seal battery (instruments/seal/battery.py): the commitment SHA256('verify-seal-v1\n' || salt || SHA256(archive)) opened under planted forgeries — each must come back REFUTED or REFUSED, never CERTIFIED — plus the determinism check (the same contents written another way re-derive the sealed digest), the date rule (an anchor dated after the claimed date refuses), the unconfirmed-anchor cases, and the one-line shell re-derivation against the Python digest; three red controls on a deliberately broken opener. Run in a temporary directory with a temporary git registry; no network, no ots client.

forgeries.forgery: one byte flipped in the archive
forgeries.reason: the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the archive: its sha256 is not the one sealed (a byte, a file or a name inside it differs)
the digest does not re-derive; what differs is the salt: salt.hex is not the salt drawn at sealing
salt.hex is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters (60 character(s))
salt.hex is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters (65 character(s), ends in a newline)
salt.hex is missing: without the salt the digest cannot be re-derived (a lost salt is an unopenable seal)
archive.tar is missing: without the bytes there is nothing to re-derive (the researcher holds it)

cases.case: the honest seal with a registry anchor
cases.reason: the archive and salt re-derive the recorded digest; 1 anchor(s) confirmed; the bytes were held by 2026-11-03

cases.case: claimed --by a date on the anchor's day
cases.reason: the archive and salt re-derive the recorded digest; 1 anchor(s) confirmed; the bytes were held by 2026-11-03 (on or before the claimed 2026-11-03)

cases.case: claimed --by a date AFTER the anchor (a later claim is weaker, still decidable)
cases.reason: the archive and salt re-derive the recorded digest; 1 anchor(s) confirmed; the bytes were held by 2026-11-03 (on or before the claimed 2026-12-01)

cases.case: an anchor dated after the claimed date (--by 2026-11-01, anchor 2026-11-03)
cases.reason: the digest re-derives and the earliest confirmed anchor is dated 2026-11-03, after the claimed 2026-11-01: possession by 2026-11-01 is not decidable from the anchors (an earlier anchor would decide it)

cases.case: no anchor at all
cases.reason: the digest re-derives, but no public anchor is in the bundle: the date is only a local claim. Decidable once `stamp` anchors it (digest.txt.ots and/or a registry commit in anchors.json)

cases.case: a registry anchor without the clone
cases.reason: the digest re-derives, but no anchor is confirmed here: no --registry <clone> given, so the commit is not read (git clone https://github.com/carlostoledo1891/cert-machine)

cases.case: an .ots present but not confirmable here
cases.reason: the digest re-derives, but no anchor is confirmed here: the ots client is not installed here (pip install opentimestamps-client), so the attestation is not read

cases.case: a registry commit that does not hold this digest
cases.reason: the digest re-derives, but no anchor is confirmed here: the digest is not in seals/registry.jsonl at that commit

red_controls.red: an opener that certifies a mismatched digest IS caught (a flipped byte comes back CERTIFIED under it)
an opener that ignores the claimed date IS caught (a date before the anchor comes back CERTIFIED under it)
an opener that tolerates a newline after the salt IS caught (bytes.fromhex strips it; the strict rule is what refuses)
